options: Falling long-run average costs as output rises
Falling total costs
Rising marginal returns in the short run
Lower prices set by government
questions.why: They are about long-run cost per unit.

questions.q: Which is an internal economy of scale?
options: A new motorway that serves the whole industry
A big firm gets cheaper loans than small ones
A local college trains workers for an industry
A rival firm closes
questions.why: Financial economies come from the firm's own size.

questions.q: Match each example to its type of economy of scale.
pairs: Larger ships cost less per container carried
A firm sells in many countries so one downturn hurts less
questions.why: These are four of the common categories.

questions.q: Which of these is a diseconomy of scale?
options: Discounts for bulk buying
Messages getting lost in a very large firm
Lower interest rates on loans
Sharing a research lab
questions.why: Communication problems raise cost per unit at very large scale.

questions.q: An L-shaped LRAC curve suggests that diseconomies of scale can be avoided.
questions.why: Costs fall and then stay low, with no upturn.

questions.q: What is the minimum efficient scale?
options: The smallest firm that can exist
The lowest output at which LRAC is at its lowest
The highest output of the firm
The output at which profit is zero
questions.why: It is where LRAC first reaches its lowest level.

questions.q: In which market is a very high MES most likely?
options: Hairdressing
Aircraft manufacturing
Window cleaning
Street food
questions.why: Huge fixed costs mean only very large output gets costs down.

questions.topic: economies of scale as a barrier to entry
questions.q: Explain how economies of scale can act as a barrier to entry.

ideas.label: Established big firms have much lower average costs
A small new firm has higher costs, so it can't compete on price

questions.model: Big established firms have lower average costs because of economies of scale. A new firm starts small with higher costs, so it cannot compete on price and may stay out of the market.
questions.why: The cost gap protects the firms already in the market.

tests.answer: Big firms have lower costs so a new firm with higher costs can't compete.
Big firms have lower average costs.
